stories.Headline: Microsoft eyes September launch for Maia 300 AI chip
stories.Summary:
Microsoft plans to launch its Maia 300 artificial intelligence chip as early as September to strengthen its custom chip capabilities. The company has been negotiating with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company to produce over 300,000 units for delivery in 2027, with hopes of eventually securing capacity for more than one million chips. Microsoft launched its first Maia chip in November 2023 and introduced the Maia 200 in January, but has lagged behind competitors like Alphabet and Amazon in scaling custom chip production as it works to reduce dependence on expensive Nvidia processors.

The new chip aims to attract major cloud customers including Anthropic to adopt the technology. Microsoft's Maia 300 will use advanced manufacturing techniques and include specialized memory components designed to enhance artificial intelligence system performance. However, component availability and ongoing negotiations with TSMC could limit production goals. The company is pursuing this expansion as Google and Amazon have already begun generating revenue from their own custom AI chips.

stories.Headline: MIT BLRU, IBM SkillsBuild Launch AI Lab to Accelerate Research and Democratise AI Skills
stories.Summary:
MIT Bengaluru and IBM have jointly launched an artificial intelligence laboratory called MIG, or MAHE Intelligence GPU, at MIT's Bengaluru campus. The facility features advanced computing infrastructure designed to make artificial intelligence research and education more accessible across India. The lab will support research in machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, computer vision, and other AI fields, while simultaneously handling 30 high-performance computing workloads. The initiative includes collaborations with industry partners and will support student innovation projects, hackathons, and startup incubation efforts.

Through IBM SkillsBuild, a free education program, MIT Bengaluru will establish an AI Learning Initiative offering workshops, bootcamps, and hands-on training in artificial intelligence and machine learning. The program specifically targets students from Tier 2 and Tier 3 institutions to bridge educational gaps and prepare learners with industry-relevant skills for an AI-focused economy. Government and industry leaders view the collaboration as significant for strengthening Karnataka's artificial intelligence ecosystem and positioning MIT Bengaluru as a leading hub for AI research and talent development.

stories.Headline: Two CityUHK scholars elected to the European Academy of Engineering in recognition of their internationally acclaimed research achievements
stories.Summary:
Two scholars from City University of Hong Kong have been elected to the European Academy of Engineering, one of the highest honors in the international engineering community. Professor Li Wen Jung from Mechanical Engineering was recognized for his pioneering work in artificial intelligence, micro and nano-systems, and robotics, with approximately 30 patents and multiple start-ups commercializing his technologies. Professor So Hing Cheung from Electrical Engineering was honored for his contributions to statistical signal processing and intelligent algorithms, particularly in areas like sparse recovery and federated learning.

Both professors have significantly contributed to the global engineering community through leadership roles and international collaborations. Professor Li previously served as Associate Provost and currently leads talent recruitment and international partnerships at the university, while also holding fellowships with major engineering organizations. Professor So was elected to China's National Academy of Artificial Intelligence in July. Their elections underscore City University of Hong Kong's growing international recognition in engineering research and innovation, joining a 2026 cohort of 147 newly elected members that includes Nobel and Turing Award laureates.

stories.Headline: Chandigarh University Students' 'Green Heart' Wins NASSCOM's Best Startup Award, Bags 5 Lakh Grant to Transform Farming with AI, Satellites & IoT
stories.Summary:
# Summary

Three final-year engineering students from Chandigarh University founded GreenHeart, an artificial intelligence-powered agriculture technology platform that recently won the Best Startup Award at Neovation 2026, organized by NASSCOM. The award came with a 500,000 rupee grant. The startup, created by Garvit Saluja, Aditya Bhandari, and Prakhar Nautiyal, uses satellite data, internet of things sensors, and AI to help farmers increase productivity while reducing water, fertilizer, and pesticide usage. The platform also detects crop diseases and stress through real-time monitoring and provides personalized crop recommendations based on soil and environmental conditions.

GreenHeart is currently conducting pilot testing with 50 farmers in Ropar and Ludhiana using hardware devices that analyze soil and water quality. The company claims farmers following its recommendations could increase crop yields and profits by 15 to 20 percent. The startup also represented Chandigarh University as a finalist in the Smart India Hackathon 2025. The founders received initial support through a government-backed seed fund of 700,000 rupees and plan to expand operations across agriculture and logistics sectors.

stories.Headline: Microsoft may reveal next-generation AI chip next month
stories.Summary:
Microsoft plans to unveil its next-generation Maia 300 artificial intelligence chip as early as September, according to reports. The company is working to reduce its dependence on expensive Nvidia processors by expanding its custom chip business. Microsoft first introduced its Maia chip in November 2023 but has lagged behind competitors like Google and Amazon in developing custom AI hardware. The new Maia 300 chip uses advanced 3-nanometer manufacturing technology and includes specialized memory to improve performance for handling large user requests.

Microsoft has discussed securing production capacity from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company for over 300,000 Maia 300 chips to be delivered in 2027. The company ultimately hopes to manufacture more than one million units and plans to encourage major cloud customers, including Anthropic, to adopt the new technology. However, component availability and ongoing negotiations could affect these production goals. Google and Amazon have already started generating significant revenue from their own custom AI chips in recent quarters.

stories.Headline: Fargo lawmaker pushes data center rules during North Dakota special session
stories.Summary:
A Fargo state senator named Tim Mathern is pushing the North Dakota Legislature to address data center regulations during an upcoming special session in the fall. Mathern plans to propose two bills, one that would ban public officials from signing non-disclosure agreements with data center developers and another that would temporarily pause new data center projects. He argues that data centers are the most pressing issue constituents raise with him and that waiting until the 2027 legislative session is too long.

However, Republican legislative leaders are skeptical about adding data center regulations to the special session, which Governor Kelly Armstrong called primarily to address kratom concerns. Senate Majority Leader David Hogue said a special session lasting three days is not the appropriate venue for this debate, noting that lawmakers established a separate interim committee to study artificial intelligence and data centers before next year's session. While Hogue expressed openness to discussing non-disclosure agreement restrictions, he believes that conversation should happen through the interim committee rather than during the special session.

stories.Headline: Sault city council supports data centre framework, rejects moratorium
stories.Summary:
Sault Ste. Marie city council rejected a moratorium on data centre development but agreed to create a policy framework to guide future projects. Two councillors proposed a motion that would have temporarily halted data centre applications while the city developed guidelines, but the majority opposed the pause, believing existing rezoning checks and balances are sufficient. The motion was withdrawn after more than an hour of debate and will be redrafted into a simplified version for the August 31 council meeting.

The debate centers on a proposed 5-megawatt data centre on Yates Avenue, a partnership between Missanabie Cree First Nation, QuantumEdge, and Protexxa that could create up to 200 jobs. Residents raised concerns about transparency and potential environmental impacts like energy consumption and noise pollution. City staff indicated they could have a draft framework policy ready for September review, with public consultation to follow. The project, distinct from massive hyperscaler facilities, is currently in early feasibility stages with potential launch between 2028 and 2029.

stories.Headline: AI evolving as core intelligence layer in India's fintech transformation: ASSOCHAM-KPMG report
stories.Summary:
India's fintech sector is undergoing significant transformation as artificial intelligence shifts from being merely a tool for automation into a strategic capability that can independently execute and enhance financial services. According to a joint report released by ASSOCHAM and KPMG at the 3rd India International Fintech Festival, the country is well positioned to lead this change due to its strong digital public infrastructure, growing connectivity, and extensive data resources. The report notes that foundational digital systems like digital identity and real-time payments create favorable conditions for widespread AI deployment.

Financial institutions are moving beyond experimental programs to company-wide adoption of AI across multiple functions including customer service, fraud prevention, compliance, and risk assessment. Industry leaders emphasized that India's next phase of fintech leadership depends not only on digital infrastructure but on how effectively intelligence is integrated throughout the ecosystem. The report identified key priorities for continued growth, including expanding computing resources, establishing strong governance structures for privacy and security, and scaling AI applications in lending and claims processing. Officials also stressed the importance of developing user-friendly interfaces in local languages to expand financial access.

stories.Headline: Presidency University and University of the West of Scotland launch innovative postgraduate programmes in Bengaluru
stories.Summary:
Presidency University in Bengaluru has partnered with the University of the West of Scotland to offer three new postgraduate programmes. Students will earn dual degrees, receiving both a Presidency award and a UWS Master's degree in 14 months without leaving India. The three programmes include Management with MBA, Public Administration with Master of Public Administration, and Artificial Intelligence with MSc Artificial Intelligence. Admissions opened for October 2026 intake at Presidency's Bengaluru campus.

The partnership allows students to study in India while accessing UK-standard education and benefiting from Presidency's industry connections for job placement. Graduates also receive five years of career support from UWS. Students have the unique opportunity to complete a two-week academic residency at UWS's Paisley campus near Glasgow. The programmes are designed to provide Indian students with both a British degree and local career networks to support their path to global employment.
